git.label: Git
git.syncHint: Commit every change, pull the remote's new commits, then push yours.
git.fetch: Fetch: check the remote for new commits
git.pull: Pull: bring in the remote's new commits
git.push: Push: send your commits to the remote
git.branchPlaceholder: Switch to or create a branch…
git.stagedHint: Staged changes go into the next commit.
git.changesHint: Changes not staged yet. Stage them to put them in the next commit.

discardConfirm.title: Discard changes?
discardConfirm.description: {count} file(s) go back to how they were in the last commit, and new files are deleted. This can't be undone.

git.commitHint: Save the staged changes as a commit: a snapshot in the history.
git.commitAllHint: Nothing is staged, so this commits every change.
git.commitPushHint: Commit, then send it to the remote.

merging.title: Merging
merging.description: Resolve each conflict: keep yours (this device's) or theirs (the remote's), or fix the file and mark it resolved. Then finish the merge, or abort to go back.

missing.title: Git isn't installed
missing.description: Vertex uses git to track and sync this workspace. Install it, then check again.
missing.macos: Vertex uses git to track and sync this workspace. Apple's developer tools include it: install them, then check again.
missing.configured: Vertex is set to use {path}, which isn't a working git. Locate another, or let Vertex find one.
missing.toolsFailed: Couldn't open the developer tools installer

notRepo.title: Not a git repository
notRepo.description: This workspace isn't tracked by git yet. Creating a repository starts tracking its changes, with a .gitignore that leaves out system files and Vertex's trash.

notRepo.title: Not a git repository
notRepo.description: This workspace isn't tracked by git.

auth.title: Couldn't sign in to the remote
auth.description: The remote refused to sign in. For an HTTPS remote, try again and enter a personal access token; for SSH, add your key to the SSH agent.

conflict.title: Merge conflicts
conflict.description: Some files changed both here and on the remote. Resolve them in the Git view's Conflicts list, then finish the merge, or abort it.

rejected.title: The remote has newer commits
rejected.description: Pull them in first, then push again.

noRemote.title: No remote to sync with
noRemote.description: This repository isn't connected to a remote yet: connect one to push.

noUpstream.title: This branch has no remote branch
noUpstream.description: It doesn't track a branch on a remote, and there's no `origin` to push it to. Push it once with `git push -u` and the remote's name.

identity.title: Git needs your name and email
identity.description: Commits record who made them. Set your name and email to commit.

git.syncChatsHint: Chats kept in this workspace are encrypted files git can't merge: when two devices change the same chat, you pick one version.

diff.againstParent: Compared with the commit before it

history.label: History
history.show: History: every commit, as a graph
history.emptyHint: Commit your changes to start the history.

signIn.title: Sign in to {host}
signIn.description: Git couldn't sign in to {host}. A personal access token lets it.
signIn.refused: {host} refused the saved token. It may have expired or lost access: enter a new one.
signIn.explain: A personal access token is a password for apps, made in your account settings on the host. Give it read and write access to your repositories.
signIn.createElsewhere: Create one in your account settings on {host}.
signIn.usernameHelp: Only if your host wants your username with tokens.
signIn.kept: Vertex keeps it in your system keychain and hands it to git only while it talks to {host}. Remove it in Settings → Git.

identity.title: Your name and email
identity.description: Every commit records who made it. These are kept in this repository only.
identity.name: Name

remote.title: Connect a remote
remote.description: A remote is a copy of this repository on a server, like GitHub. Your devices sync through it: each pushes its commits there and pulls the others'.
remote.empty: Make it private, and leave it empty: no README, .gitignore or license, so the first push goes straight in. Then copy its HTTPS URL here.

push.title: Push your notes
push.description: Vertex commits every file and pushes the commit to the remote. If the remote asks you to sign in, Vertex helps you make a token.

sync.title: Sync
sync.description: One click keeps your devices in step: it commits every change, pulls the remote's new commits, then pushes yours.

branch.title: Branch
branch.description: A branch is a line of work. Switch branches here, or type a name to start a new one.

aheadBehind.title: Ahead and behind
aheadBehind.description: Commits of yours the remote doesn't have yet (up arrow), and commits on the remote you haven't pulled (down arrow).

remoteActions.title: Fetch, pull and push
remoteActions.description: Fetch checks the remote for new commits, pull brings them into your files, push sends your commits to the remote.

list.title: Changes and staged
list.description: Changes lists the files you edited since the last commit. Stage (plus) the ones that go into the next commit: they move to Staged. Click a file to see what changed.

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: A commit saves the staged changes (or every change, when nothing is staged) as one step in the history, with a message saying what changed.

history.title: History
history.description: Every commit, branch by branch: select one to see what it changed.

clone.title: Clone a workspace
clone.description: Copy a repository from a remote into a new folder and open it as a workspace.
clone.name: Folder name

conflicts.label: Conflicts
conflicts.hint: Files changed both here and on the remote. Keep one side, or open the file, fix the parts git marked and mark it resolved.
conflicts.markersConfirm: {count} file(s) still have conflict markers: {files}. Mark them resolved anyway?

rebasing.title: Rebasing
rebasing.description: Your commits are being replayed onto the remote's. Resolve each conflict: keep yours (this device's) or theirs (the remote's), or fix the file and mark it resolved. Then continue; a later commit may stop again. Or abort to go back.

settings.title: Git
settings.tokensDescription: Personal access tokens for HTTPS remotes, saved when a remote refused to sign in. They stay in your system keychain; git gets one only while it talks to its host, and your own credential helpers aren't asked then.
settings.noTokens: No saved tokens. Vertex asks for one when a remote refuses to sign in.
settings.failed: Couldn't read or change the saved tokens

autoSync.title: Auto-sync
autoSync.description: Keeps this computer's workspaces in step without pressing Sync: commits every change, pulls and pushes. It waits during a merge or rebase and pauses after a sign-in failure until a sync from the Git view works. A trusted workspace can have its own.
autoSync.intervalDescription: How often a workspace window syncs while it's open.
autoSync.pullOnFocus: Pull when the window gets focus
autoSync.pullOnFocusDescription: Brings in the remote's new commits when you come back to the window (at most once a minute).
autoSync.untrusted: This workspace's auto-sync applies once its folder is trusted.

commitMessages.whenEmpty: Write a message for an empty box
commitMessages.whenEmptyDescription: Commit or Sync with nothing typed asks the model for a message. Off, they commit as "Update N file(s)".
commitMessages.autoSyncDescription: Auto-sync's commits get a message from the model (sending the diff on every sync). Off, they're "Update N file(s)".

commitMessageFeature.label: Commit messages
commitMessageFeature.description: Writes commit messages from the changes, in the style of the repository's recent ones: the Git view's sparkle button, and when you set it below, an empty message box and auto-sync. The diff is sent to the model.
